nodes.name: NF Cleaning
nodes.procedure: Firstly, a piece of NF was treated with HCl, acetone, and deionized water by ultrasonic cleaning sequentially before use.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, a piece of NF was treated with HCl, acetone, and deionized water by ultrasonic cleaning sequentially before use.

nodes.name: FeMoO4 Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: A piece of NF was then immersed into 30 mL of deionized water containing 2.5 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 2.5 mmol Na2MoO4·2H2O, and 0.24 mol urea. The mixture was ultrasonicated for 30 min and then hydrothermally treated at 100°C for 6 h. After cooling down to room temperature, the NF deposited with FeMoO4 nanorod array was taken out and repeatedly washed with ethanol and water.

nodes.name: RuO2/NF Preparation
nodes.procedure: 5 mg RuO2 was added in a solution containing 30 μL of Nafion, 485 μL of ethanol, and 485 μL of deionized water with the aid of ultrasonication (0.5 h) to form a homogeneous ink (5 mg·mL⁻¹). 280 μL of catalyst ink was then dropped onto a piece of cleaned NF (1 cm × 1 cm) with a loading mass of 1.4 mg·cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows three diffraction peaks corresponding to crystalline Ni phase and a broadened peak at 21.35° indicating amorphous FeMoO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern of FeMoO4/NF (Fig. 1(b)) shows three diffraction peaks (marked with '*'), corresponding to the crystalline phase of Ni (JCPDS No. 04-0850). Apart from that, a broadened diffraction peak at 21.35 was observed, indicating that the synthesized FeMoO4 is amorphous.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman characteristic peaks at 812 and 929 cm⁻¹ correspond to asymmetric and symmetric stretching modes of MoO₄²⁻, proving the FeMoO4 structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the Raman characteristic peaks could be observed at 812 and 929 cm⁻¹, which correspond to the asymmetric stretching and symmetric stretching modes of MoO₄²⁻, respectively, proving the structure of FeMoO4 (Fig. 1(c)).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show FeMoO4 nanorods uniformly distributed on NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images depicted in Figs. 1(d) and 1(e) display that FeMoO4 nanorods were uniformly distributed on NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Fe 2p peaks at 724.53 eV (Fe 2p1/2) and 712.84 eV (Fe 2p3/2) for Fe²⁺, Mo 3d peaks at 235.22 eV (Mo 3d3/2) and 232.06 eV (Mo 3d5/2) for Mo⁶⁺, and O 1s peaks at 529.91 eV (metal-oxygen) and 531.12 eV (adsorbed oxygen).
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS survey spectrum (Fig. 2(a)) further evidences the existence of Fe, Mo, and O. In Fe 2p region, the peaks at 724.53 and 712.84 eV are attributed to Fe 2p1/2 and Fe 2p3/2 of Fe²⁺, respectively (Fig. 2(b)). Besides, XPS Mo 3d peaks can be deconvoluted into Mo 3d3/2 at 235.22 eV and Mo 3d5/2 at 232.06 eV, confirming the oxidation state of Mo specie is +6 (Fig. 2(c)). In addition, the O 1s spectra at 529.91 and 531.12 eV are assigned to metal–oxygen bond and adsorbed oxygen, respectively (Fig. 2(d)).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates from 20-100 mV/s gives Cdl value corresponding to ECSA of 107.5 cm², the largest among compared electrodes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The double-layer capacitance (Cdl) values of FeMoO4/NF, RuO2/NF, and NF were measured via cyclic voltammetry (CV) at different scan rates from 20-100 mV⋅s⁻¹ in 1 M KOH. ... FeMoO4/NF shows the largest ECSA value (107.5 cm²) compared to RuO2/NF (40.68 cm²) and NF (21.69 cm²).
